questions.stem: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to: transparent
questions.explanation: Opaque means not allowing light through, the direct opposite of transparent.

questions.stem: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to: scarce
questions.explanation: Scarce means in short supply; plentiful means existing in large quantities.

questions.stem: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to: optimistic
questions.explanation: An optimistic person expects good outcomes; a pessimistic one expects bad outcomes.

questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to: diligent
questions.explanation: A diligent person shows steady, careful effort: hardworking.

questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to: commence
questions.explanation: To commence is to start or begin.

questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to: abundant
questions.explanation: Abundant means existing in large quantities: plentiful.

questions.stem: Neither the teacher nor the students ______ present.
questions.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, students (plural), so 'were'.

questions.stem: Bola, as well as her friends, ______ coming to the party.
questions.explanation: 'As well as her friends' is a parenthetical; the verb agrees with the main subject Bola (singular).

questions.stem: He has been good ______ mathematics since primary school.
questions.explanation: The fixed collocation is 'good at' a subject or skill.

questions.stem: The man was accused ______ theft.
questions.explanation: The fixed collocation is 'accused of' an offence.

questions.stem: The thief was arrested ______ the police.
questions.explanation: 'By' marks the agent in a passive construction.

questions.stem: She has been living in Lagos ______ 2019.
questions.explanation: 'Since' introduces a point in time; 'for' introduces a duration.

questions.stem: After the failed deal, Chidi found himself in hot water. This means he was
questions.explanation: The idiom 'in hot water' means in trouble or difficulty.

questions.stem: Ada let the cat out of the bag. This means she
questions.explanation: 'Let the cat out of the bag' means to disclose a secret.

questions.stem: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling has double 'c' and double 'm': accommodation.

questions.stem: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Embarrass has double 'r' and double 's'.

questions.stem: Choose the passive form of: The boy kicked the ball.
options: The ball was kicked by the boy.
The ball is kicking the boy.
The boy was kicked by the ball.
questions.explanation: Passive voice: object becomes subject + be + past participle + by + agent.

questions.stem: If I ______ rich, I would build a school in my village.
questions.explanation: Second conditional (unreal present) uses 'were' for all persons in formal English.

questions.stem: She asked me where I ______ from.
questions.explanation: In reported speech the present 'come' backsifts to the past 'came'.

questions.stem: Choose the word that rhymes with: book
questions.explanation: Both 'book' and 'look' carry the same short vowel sound /ʊ/.
